newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends well bid, risk seen on upside.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends well bid, risk seen on upside.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed with a bid tone on Monday, buoyed by solid offshore buying and news that publisher Wilson and Horton was facing a takeover offer from a subsidiary of Ireland's Independent Newspapers.
The Kiwi ended at US$0.6955/62, up from 0.6941/48 at the open. On its Trade-Weighted Index, the Kiwi closed firmer at 66.26 from 66.14.
Dealers said that although the Japanese market had been closed for a national holiday, several houses had remained active and placed some sizeable buy orders for the Kiwi.
"And I think the market was a bit short," one dealer said. "It looks pretty bid really."
He said the offer for Wilson and Horton, while not a direct influence on the currency yet, had improved sentiment.

"That's certainly a positive for the currency. (Tony) O'Reilly (the largest shareholder of Independent Newspapers) will probably have to buy the Kiwi. Although it will be a few days before they actually buy it, it's probably going to be up to NZ$400 million, and so that's just another positive," he said.
Dealers said there had also been rumours that tonight's TV3 political opinion poll would be good news for the conservative National Party government, and therefore for the currency.
"There were rumours earlier that it could come out all right for the right-wing over the left-wing and that some of the smaller parties could do well," a dealer said.
The right-wing Christian Coalition and ACT parties are seen as possible supporters for National in a right-of-centre coalition government.
A general election will be held on October 12 under a new system of proportional representation, which is likely to produce a coalition or minority government.

Recent polls show that the three main opposition parties together command a greater percentage of the vote than the government and the market fears that a left-wing coalition would cause a capital flight out of New Zealand.
But dealers said the risk for the Kiwi remained on the upside in the short term. They expected the currency to trade a 0.6945-75 range overnight.
